topic: Grover's Algorithm: Finding a Needle in a Quantum Haystack
target_audience: University students with a basic understanding of linear algebra and quantum states.

sections.title: The Classical Search Problem
lecture_lines: Searching an unsorted database is a fundamental challenge.
We must check items one by one classically.
Finding one item among N takes O(N) time.
animations: Display a grid of 10 closed treasure chests labeled 'Search Space' in #FFFFFF.
Highlight chests one by one in #FFFF00 to show Alice checking them sequentially.
Change the 7th chest to #FFD700 and display 'O(N) Complexity' in #00FF00.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Quantum Superposition
lecture_lines: Quantum computers use superposition to represent all states.
Applying Hadamard gates creates an equal probability distribution.
Every possible answer now exists in parallel.
animations: Show 10 vertical bars of equal height in #00BFFF with 'Probability Amplitude' label.
Pulse all bars simultaneously in #FFFFFF to represent a Hadamard transform.
Maintain the uniform heights to show the system is in a state of 'all chests partially open'.

sections.title: Step 1: The Oracle (Phase Inversion)
lecture_lines: We use an Oracle to identify the correct answer.
The Oracle recognizes the target state without measuring.
It flips the sign of the target's probability amplitude.
This process is known as phase inversion.
Other states remain completely unchanged by the Oracle.
animations: Show a collection of white vertical bars representing quantum states.
Highlight one specific bar (the 4th) with the label 'Target' in #FFD700.
Slowly flip the target bar across the X-axis so it points downwards.
Change the color of the flipped bar to #FF4500 and show a dashed line at Y=0.
Pulse the other white bars to show they are unaffected.

sections.title: Step 2: The Diffusion Operator (Inversion about the Mean)
lecture_lines: Next, we apply the Grover diffusion operator.
It performs an inversion about the average amplitude.
The target's negative amplitude is pushed far above average.
Meanwhile, all incorrect amplitudes are significantly reduced.
This amplification makes the target state much more likely.
animations: Display the bars from the previous step (one down, others up).
Draw a horizontal dashed line in #7CFC00 representing the 'Mean' amplitude.
Show the target bar's distance from the mean line to prepare for the flip.
Flip all bars across the mean line; the target bar becomes very tall.
Highlight the tall target bar in #00FF00 to show its dominance.

sections.title: The Geometric View: Vector Rotation
lecture_lines: We can visualize Grover's algorithm as a geometric rotation.
The quantum state starts far from the target vector.
Each iteration rotates the state toward the solution.
The Oracle and Diffusion together create this rotation.
The state vector gradually aligns with the target state.
animations: Display a 2D plane with white axes labeled $|s\rangle$ and $|w\rangle$.
Draw the initial state vector $|\psi\rangle$ in #FF00FF close to the $|s\rangle$ axis.
Show the vector rotating by an angle $\theta$ toward the $|w\rangle$ axis.
Overlay a text box 'Oracle + Diffusion' to show the cause of rotation.
Show the vector landing almost perfectly on the $|w\rangle$ axis.

sections.title: Quantum Speedup & Conclusion
lecture_lines: We only need roughly square root of N iterations.
This provides a massive quadratic speedup over classical methods.
Measuring the system now reveals the correct answer.
animations: Show a comparison table of 'Classical: 1,000,000' vs 'Quantum: 1,000' in #FFFFFF.
Display a green progress bar filling to '31 steps' to represent $O(\sqrt{N})$ speedup.
Fade in a solid Golden Key icon in #FFD700 to represent the final measurement.
